I tested the current main commit `1c0152c9106514622a641c17adc7520af45ebc6a` with Cargo 1.100.0 on Linux.

The feature graphs still differ. For example, `smallvec` has no enabled features in the geometry tree. The app tree adds `const_generics,const_new`. The UI tree also adds `serde,union`. `serde`, `tracing`, `num-traits`, and compression dependencies also have different feature sets.

However, I did not reproduce repeated library compilation in the warm prebuilds:

1. `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=3 cargo xtask gate batch --only 'debug build'` passed all 11 current prebuilds.
2. An immediate `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=3 cargo xtask gate batch` passed all 11 prebuilds without a workspace `Compiling` line.
3. A second warm run, with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`, also passed all 11 prebuilds without a workspace `Compiling` line.

The current plan has 11 prebuilds because it includes gcode and gpu. I stopped the three-job attempt during suites. The six-job full batch is still running. These prebuild results are not a full-batch pass.

The logs show cache reuse. They do not prove that all roots share one rlib variant. Feature differences alone do not prove repeated warm compilation either. I have not changed the manifests or the build plan for this unobserved warm-cache symptom. I have not opened a PR or closed this issue.

claim withdrawn - issue is free again.

Ownership released: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3191#issuecomment-7204253991
Role: writer
Owner: seelesturm / coder / t_e0d083b3
Final head: 1c0152c9106514622a641c17adc7520af45ebc6a
Result: stopped without a patch; the warm prebuilds reused cached libraries. Raw feature trees and build logs are preserved for independent review.

Final validation note: I stopped the six-job batch before completion to keep this investigation bounded. It is not a full-gate pass. The unchanged main tree failed motion suites: finish3d_hop_height. A focused recheck reproduced three failing tests with unexpected RapidInPart findings. I did not change that code. The two completed warm prebuild phases each have 11 successful build logs and zero compilation lines. No patch or PR was published.

Correction to my earlier diagnostic: the warm logs prove cache reuse, not the required single shared rlib. The issue is not fixed.

I checked the active `compiler-artifact` records from all 11 completed prebuilds. Geometry and cl each select four rlib variants. Tools, post, sim, and motion each select three. App selects two. Kernel selects five, including its expected truck variant.

For geometry, the compiler, profile, target, own features, config, and flags match across the four roots. The dependency fingerprints differ. I matched the parent fingerprint values to the selected child units, rather than counting old directories or combining host and target packages.

Two proven paths are:

- `camcraft_geometry -> camcraft_kernel -> solidcore_tess -> spade -> smallvec`
- `camcraft_geometry -> clipper2_rust -> num_traits`

Target smallvec features change from none in geometry to `const_generics,const_new` in app and `const_generics,const_new,serde,union` in UI. Target num-traits features change from `default,std` to `default,i128,std`, then `default,i128,libm,std`.

The existing workspace manifests have no direct smallvec, num-traits, or spade dependency. The existing solidcore dependencies expose no forwarding feature for these differences. Clipper2 exposes only `default` and `using_z`. A serde/tracing-only alignment would therefore leave required lower-crate variants distinct.

My bounded contribution scope does not permit new direct dependency edges or changes to truck isolation. I also checked a grouped-build alternative with a small local Cargo fixture. Grouped direct execution and standalone per-package execution select different dependency features and can produce different test results. This confirms why the current gate rejects multi-package artifact recording. It is not evidence of a CamCraft algorithm failure.

I stopped at that scope boundary without a patch or PR. A complete solution needs additional feature-control edges or a consistent decision about grouped builds and the cargo fallback. The original acceptance requirement is clear and remains unmet. The earlier claim stays withdrawn; the issue remains free. I did not repeat the full batch or change algorithms.

I exercised the approved feature-control approach on current main `903e420b3a6443330233d3e58386d84100a21c5e`.

A bounded geometry probe added native dev-only controls for eight packages already present transitively. It aligned the target feature sets of smallvec, num-traits, serde, tracing, memchr, crc32fast, simd-adler32 and either. No package version changed. A normal geometry build still reused its original cached library.

The final diagnostic builds succeeded, but the active non-test libraries remained different:

- Geometry root: geometry `5e301bc01990dbf6`, kernel `308f7147a74037d0`.
- UI root: geometry `c2fe8c42a31e801b`, kernel `fe7fd8d8afdd8cb1`.

The kernel paths both have `default`, not `truck`. Their compiler, profile, target, own features and flags match. The remaining fingerprint paths reach host syn 3.0.8 through serde_derive and host syn 2.0.119 through tracing-attributes. Target dev controls do not align those host contexts.

A separate necessary difference appears directly under the actual non-test post library. Standalone post selects rustix 1.1.5 with `alloc,default,fs,std`. The UI context selects `alloc,default,event,fs,net,pipe,process,shm,std,system,time` for that same package and profile. Full alignment therefore also requires a decision about widening the native post-test OS/network surface. My contribution scope excludes that widening merely for deduplication.

I stopped before a broad batch. I saved the incomplete probe and exact artifact/fingerprint evidence, then removed the probe from the checkout. No complete fix, commit, push, PR, full-gate pass or cross-platform result is claimed. The previous baseline test failures remain separate. This result does not satisfy the single-rlib acceptance.

claim withdrawn - issue is free again.
